question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=5\sqrt[3]{x}+3
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=5\sqrt[3]{y}+3.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5\sqrt[3]{y}+3 \\ 5\sqrt[3]{y} & =x-3 \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =\frac{1}{5}(x-3) \\ (\sqrt[3]{y})^{3} & ={(\frac{1}{5}(x-3))}^{3} \\ y & =\frac{1}{125}(x-3)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{125}(x-3)^{3}.
$$
